cards.explanation: The answer is those who ruin kings. Lemuel's mother says, "Do not spend your strength on women or your vigor on those who ruin kings." (Proverbs 31:3) So the warning is about where a king pours his vigor, and she names the ones who ruin kings. Lemuel's mother is not mincing words here, friends, and I respect it.

The answer is to drink wine. Lemuel's mother tells him, "It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine…" (Proverbs 31:4) She says it twice, so she means it. When a line gets said twice, you can bet it matters. I wouldn't ask for a third round.

The answer is that they forget what is decreed. Lemuel's mother says it's "…lest they drink and forget what is decreed…" (Proverbs 31:5) A ruler is supposed to remember what is decreed. I can't even keep track of my own oven timer on a good day, so a king with a whole kingdom has a lot to remember.

The answer is oppressed. The ruler who forgets ends up "…depriving all the oppressed of justice." (Proverbs 31:5) The oppressed are the ones who pay when a ruler forgets, friends. I think that's why she wants Lemuel's head clear.

The answer is his poverty. Lemuel's mother says, "Let him drink and forget his poverty…" (Proverbs 31:7) Her words are for the one who is perishing and the one who is bitter in soul. Notice who she's looking at: someone hurting, not a king on his throne.

The answer is voice. Lemuel's mother says, "Open your mouth for those with no voice…" (Proverbs 31:8) A king has a voice that carries, so she tells him to use it for people who don't have one. That's a mighty big job for a mouth, bakers.

The answer is True. Lemuel's mother says, "Open your mouth for those with no voice, for the cause of all the dispossessed." (Proverbs 31:8) The dispossessed are right there in the verse. Those with no voice and all the dispossessed are the people she points the king toward.

The answer is judge righteously. Lemuel's mother says, "Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy." (Proverbs 31:9) That's three instructions in one verse: speak up, judge righteously, and defend the poor and needy. She hands the king the whole list in one breath, friends.

The answer is False. Her last line is, "Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy." (Proverbs 31:9) She strings three things together: the king speaks up, he judges righteously, and he defends. Both his speaking and his judging are aimed at the cause of the poor and needy, and the rich aren't named at all.
